title: Recognizing Depression and Anxiety
hook: Depression and anxiety are among the most common — and most treatable — health conditions. Knowing the signs is the first step to getting help that works.
key_points: Depression is more than sadness: persistent low mood, loss of interest, fatigue, and changes in sleep or appetite lasting weeks.
Anxiety becomes a disorder when worry is excessive, hard to control, and interferes with daily life.
Both are real medical conditions, not personal failings, and both respond well to treatment.
If symptoms persist for more than two weeks or affect daily function, it's time to talk to a professional.
content_html: Feeling down or worried is part of being human. But when those feelings settle in and start running the show, they may be something more — and recognizing the difference is what gets people to effective help.
extra_html: The National Institute of Mental Health describes depression as a persistent low or empty mood, a loss of interest in things once enjoyed, fatigue, and changes in sleep, appetite, or concentration that last at least two weeks and interfere with daily life. Anxiety is normal in stressful moments, but an anxiety disorder involves worry that's excessive, hard to switch off, and disruptive — sometimes with physical symptoms like a racing heart or restlessness. NIMH stresses that these are common medical conditions, not character flaws, and that they're highly treatable through therapy, medication, or both. The practical takeaway: if symptoms last more than a couple of weeks or get in the way of work, relationships, or daily routines, that's the signal to reach out to a clinician rather than wait it out.

related.title: What Mental Health Really Means
related.hook: Mental health isn't just the absence of illness — it's being able to cope with life's stresses, work, learn, and contribute. Everyone has it, and it can be cared for.

related.title: What Stress Does to Your Body
related.hook: A jolt of stress is useful — it sharpens you for a real threat. The problem is when the alarm never switches off, and the body pays for staying on high alert.

related.title: When a Symptom Needs a Doctor
related.hook: Most everyday symptoms pass on their own. The skill worth having is recognizing the red flags that mean don't wait — call for help now.

flashcards.prompt: What separates clinical depression from ordinary sadness?
flashcards.back_html: Depression is persistent — low mood, loss of interest, fatigue, and changes in sleep or appetite that last most of the day, for two weeks or more, and interfere with daily life.

flashcards.prompt: When does normal worry cross into an anxiety disorder?

choices.text: When it's excessive, hard to control, and disrupts daily life
Any time you feel nervous before an event
Only if you also feel physically ill

flashcards.explanation_html: Everyone feels anxious sometimes; it becomes a disorder when the worry is excessive, persistent, difficult to control, and interferes with functioning.
